Riyadh · ENT · Facial Plastic Surgery

A nose that breathes well and looks natural

I'm Dr. Abdulelah Alqahtani, a Consultant ENT and Facial Plastic Surgeon in Riyadh. My focus is nasal surgery, both aesthetic and functional, because how the nose looks and how it works are inseparable.

Areas of care

  • Rhinoplasty

    Reshaping the nose in harmony with the face, while preserving or improving breathing.

    Read more

  • Revision rhinoplasty

    Correcting the shape or breathing after previous nose surgery.

    Read more

  • Septoplasty & turbinates

    Treating chronic nasal blockage from the inside, without changing the outside.

    Read more

  • Endoscopic sinus surgery

    Treating chronic sinusitis and polyps through the nose, with no external incisions.

    Read more

  • General ENT clinic

    Diagnosis and treatment of ear, nose and throat problems in adults, from nasal blockage and allergy to tonsils and snoring.

How I work

  • Form and function together

    Every rhinoplasty plan starts with an assessment of breathing. A nose that looks good but doesn't breathe well is not a successful result.

  • A result that looks like you

    The aim is a nose in balance with your own features, not one template applied to everyone.

  • An honest consultation

    I explain what can and can't be achieved, the risks and the alternatives, before any decision. Sometimes surgery isn't the answer.

Your journey, step by step

  1. Consultation

    History, endoscopic examination where needed, photographs and a conversation about your goals.

  2. Plan

    A written plan covering the procedure, preparation and expected cost, with an illustrative digital simulation for aesthetic cases.

  3. Surgery

    Performed in an equipped hospital; most patients go home the same day or after one night.

  4. Follow-up

    Scheduled follow-up visits until the result settles, and a clear way to reach us with questions.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a referral to book?

Private clinics usually don't require one. If you're using insurance, check your policy terms before the appointment.

Does insurance cover nasal surgery?

Functional procedures such as septoplasty and sinus surgery may be covered depending on your policy and diagnosis. Purely cosmetic surgery is usually not covered.

What should I bring to the first consultation?

Any previous reports or scans, a list of your medications, and the operative report from any previous nasal surgery if you have it.

Do you treat children?

My main focus is adults. It depends on the case, so please get in touch to ask.

Considering this procedure?

It starts with an unhurried consultation: an examination, a conversation about your goals, and a clear plan for your case.
